rationale: Lens: scope and split honesty. The 129/129b boundary is real (129 = the verbs that decide readiness: next/MF-2/MF-3/override + ADR rider; 129b = the terminal mutation verbs complete/impl-approve: #234 OWNERSHIP ref, #244 atomicity, merge_strategy) and the Impacted Domains claim (workflow + execution) is honest — every in-scope path is under those two OWNERSHIP.yaml manifests. The S0 deferral is justified (unowned path, different review centre). But three scope claims do not hold at the reviewed commit 7a490064: (1) #250 was handed to the 'spec-129 follow-on' by name in spec 128 § Non-Goals and 129 drops it to 'Also not goals' with no home and no count; (2) #232 is declared closed 'on evidence' by causes that do not match its reproduction — its dependency is a same-spec bead (cause 1 cannot apply) and it was one 6/6 round (cause 3 as written, two lexically-sorted rounds, is not its shape). The mechanism that DOES match is the one #233 names in its title: `mindspec complete`'s own landing commit never equals the panel-reviewed SHA, so the single registration vetoes — and internal/lifecycle/landed.go returns that contradiction BEFORE the surviving-tip and binding legs run. After R4.3 that shape PASSES only when leg (d) (binding, written since spec 121) or (b) exists; a binding-less merge becomes *LandedMergeNoEvidence → `mindspec reattest`, which #233 (deferred to spec 130) says is unsatisfiable. The spec must say that, not 'closed by R4.1–R4.4'; (3) the deliverable count is internally inconsistent (Background: 6+1+1+1+1 = 10; OQ-1: 7+3+1 = 11) and counts neither R7 nor the ADR-0041 amendment nor #250, and 'seven code beads' understates R1 and R6 (each 4–5 sub-requirements across 3+ packages with 5–6 named tests; spec 128 planned 10 beads for a comparable surface). None of this needs a split — the fix is honest wording and one routed issue — so REQUEST_CHANGES, not REJECT.
concrete_changes_required: Route GH #250 explicitly: either add it to 129b's Non-Goals list (it is #244's family by the issue's own words — a multi-step terminal mutation with no intermediate stop) or name another home; include it in the cluster count. Remove it from the unhomed 'Also not goals' sentence.

Rewrite Background D.3 and R4.5 so the #232 disposition names the mechanism that matches its reproduction: a single registration whose reviewed_head_sha differs from the merge's second parent because `mindspec complete` commits after review (#233's class), returned as a contradiction before the tip/binding legs — not 'cause 1 or cause 3'. State the closure condition honestly: after R4.3 the #232 shape PASSES via leg (d) (merge-time binding, post-spec-121) or (b); with neither it resolves to *LandedMergeNoEvidence → `mindspec reattest`, whose unsatisfiability is #233/spec 130. Cross-reference #233 from R4.5 and keep #232 linked from the spec-130 reattest spec for that residual.

Make AC-11's #232 leg the real shape, not only 'remote-tracking ref behind local tip → PASS': (i) one registration with reviewed_head_sha ≠ second parent AND a landed binding present → FindLandedMerge CONFIRMS via (d) and the panel leg is reported non-corroborating (red-on-revert: today it contradicts); (ii) the same with NO binding and no surviving branch → *LandedMergeNoEvidence naming the candidate, never the zero-candidate sentence. Keep the local-ahead-of-remote leg as the regression guard it already is.

Fix the deliverable arithmetic so Background and OQ-1 agree, count R7 (ADR-0045) and the R4.3 ADR-0041 amendment as deliverables, and state the bead count as a plan-time estimate range (e.g. 7–10) rather than asserting 'seven code beads' as the compression argument. If the gate wants compression relief, state the natural split as R6 (override UX; coupled only through the readiness report), not R4 (R4.1 depends on R1.1's predicate) — update OQ-1's re-open clause accordingly. No split is required by this reviewer.

Disposition #239's reported menu defect: cmd/mindspec/next.go still prints `mindspec next --spec=<number>` after listing spec IDs, and `--spec=1` is rejected. Either fold a one-line fix into R1 (print the listed `--spec=<spec-id>` form) with an AC, or add it to Non-Goals with a named home. It is currently neither fixed nor mentioned.

Remove the Impacted Domains option to mirror R1.4's consumer rule into `ms-spec-autopilot` skill prose, or restate it as ADR-0045 §5 staging (target gate/config ID + removal date). As written the spec that lands ADR-0045 permits what ADR-0045 §4 forbids ('a skill does not contain a rule').

Give ADR-0045 Implementation-order step 1 (the S0 rule table) ONE named home in both the spec's Non-Goals and the ADR text (spec 130 or a dedicated governance spec — pick), or mark it explicitly 'unassigned'; an Accepted ADR whose first step floats between two homes is a scope gap. Also either add a one-line 'Amended by ADR-0045' pointer to ADR-0040 §1 to In Scope (repo precedent: the spec-123 amendment is written INTO ADR-0040; spec 121/125 amendments are written INTO ADR-0041) or record why ADR-0040's text is left untouched.

findings.title: #250 silently orphaned from the inherited cluster
findings.detail: Spec 128 § Non-Goals: 'Deferred to a spec-129 follow-on … #255, #239, #232, #234, #244, #250'. Spec 129 § Non-Goals assigns #234/#244/merge_strategy to a named 129b, then says 'Also not goals: #250 (blessing merge-then-complete)' with no follow-up spec named. The Background's 'ten independently reviewable deliverables' and OQ-1's enumeration both omit it. #250 itself says it is #244's family ('a multi-step terminal mutation with no intermediate stop … at the epic level rather than the bead level'), so 129b is the obvious home; the spec just has to say so. Every other inherited issue has a named owner; this one has none.

findings.title: #232 is closed by causes that do not fit its reproduction; the fitting cause is the #233 class this spec defers to spec 130
findings.detail: Spec text: '#232's reproduction … fits cause 1 (the dependency edge's target) or cause 3 (a stale panel registration). It is closed by this spec's fixes with that evidence (R4.5, AC-11).' Checked against the issue: the failing dependency is bead 1 of the SAME spec, merged by `mindspec complete` (so cause 1 — a non-member dependency — cannot apply), after one 6/6 panel round (so cause 3 as written — two per-round slugs with the stale one sorting first — is not its shape). What does fit: internal/lifecycle/landed.go FindLandedMerge evaluates the panel leg first and RETURNS the exact-equality contradiction before the surviving-tip and binding legs are consulted (verified in the function body at 7a490064), and GH #233's title states the general fact: 'mindspec complete's own landing commit always differs from any panel-reviewed SHA'. So a single, non-stale registration vetoes on every normal completion; evaluateMF3 then prints the zero-candidate sentence (cause 4). R4.3 (non-corroborating set) is the right fix, but what happens next depends on leg (d): a merge made since spec 121 carries a binding and PASSES; #232 was filed on 0.12.0 (pre-binding) with the bead branch already deleted, so the same state resolves to *LandedMergeNoEvidence → 'run mindspec reattest' — and #233 says reattest cannot corroborate it either. Claiming '#232 closed on evidence' while routing its actual residual to spec 130 without saying so is the scope dishonesty this lens exists to catch. The OQ-3 text half-acknowledges the structural case but defers it to the plan; the disposition sentence and AC-11's fourth leg (which, as a plain 'remote behind local → PASS' fixture, is green today and tests nothing about #232's real shape) do not.

findings.title: Deliverable count is inconsistent and undercounted
findings.detail: Background: 'ten independently reviewable deliverables: six readiness/selection fixes (A–F), the OWNERSHIP-ref fix, impl approve atomicity, the dead merge_strategy key, and the ADR-0045 rule table' = 6+1+1+1+1 = 10. OQ-1: 'ten reviewable deliverables (A–F = 7 code beads counting D as two; G, H, I = 3; S0 = 1 doc)' = 7+3+1 = 11. Neither counts R7 (ADR-0045 itself, which the spec lands), the R4.3 ADR-0041 amendment, or #250. 'Seven code beads' is also optimistic: R1 has five sub-requirements spanning internal/next, cmd/mindspec, internal/instruct and the phase derivation with five named tests; R6 has four spanning cobra flag redesign, evidence-file I/O, marker schema, ready-check read-back, re-claim subset rule and docs with six named tests; spec 128 (comparable surface, 6 requirement groups) planned 10 beads. Splitting is not needed — the spec is cohesive around one theme and R4.1 depends on R1.1's predicate, so OQ-1's proposed 129c (R4 alone) would ADD coupling — but the count must be honest and the natural relief valve (R6) named.

findings.title: #239's `--spec=<number>` menu defect is live and unmentioned
findings.detail: GH #239 § Minor reports that the ambiguity menu says `mindspec next --spec=<number>` but `--spec=1` fails. At 7a490064 cmd/mindspec/next.go still prints `mindspec next --spec=<number>` after listing `idrender.Spec(s.SpecID)` rows (the IDs are right there). Spec 128 did not fix it (no mention in its spec.md); spec 129 neither fixes it nor lists it under Non-Goals. The lens asks whether anything in #239 is silently dropped: this is. One-line fix or one-line Non-Goal — either is fine, silence is not.

findings.title: Impacted Domains permits a skill-prose rule the spec's own ADR-0045 forbids
findings.detail: Impacted Domains: '`plugins/mindspec/**` and `.claude/skills/**` only if the plan chooses to mirror R1.4's one-line consumer rule into `ms-spec-autopilot`'. ADR-0045 §4 (landed Accepted by R7): 'A skill does not contain … a rule ("must", "never", "only after")'; §5 allows staging only with a target gate/config ID and a removal date. The spec that lands the ADR should not license an unstaged violation of it in the same document. Strike the option or restate it as §5 staging.

findings.title: S0 deferral justified, but the ADR's first step has two candidate homes and ADR-0040 is amended without being touched
findings.detail: The S0 rule table is correctly deferred (pure policy, `.mindspec/policy/` claimed by no OWNERSHIP.yaml — verified: the four manifests claim internal/**, cmd/**, plugins/**, .claude/**, .gitignore, scripts/bd-jsonl-merge-driver.sh, .golangci.yml, ci.yml and themselves). But Non-Goals says 'spec 130 or a dedicated governance spec' and ADR-0045's Implementation order leaves steps 1, 5, 6 and 7 without a spec number while steps 2–4 have one. Pick a home for step 1 or mark it unassigned in both places. Separately, ADR-0045 declares 'Amends: ADR-0040 §1 (the L4 definition)' but the commit touches only ADR-0045 and spec.md, and ADR-0040 is not in § In Scope; repo precedent writes amendments INTO the amended ADR (ADR-0040's 2026-07-23 spec-123 amendment block; ADR-0041's Spec 121 and Spec 125 blocks). A one-line pointer in ADR-0040 §1 is the cheap, conventional fix.

findings.title: Spec-128's deferred #255 face is answered and no consumer is silently broken
findings.detail: Spec 128 deferred to 129 'whether a spec-scoped emptiness signal may ever be consumed as spec-is-done by autopilot/orchestration'. R1.4 answers it (never; the derived phase printed on every empty-set result is the signal) and puts the rule at L3. I checked the consumer: plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-spec-autopilot/SKILL.md stops on 'All spec-owned beads closed', not on `next` emptiness, and ms-bead-cycle step 0 picks by `--pick K`, so changing the empty-set text and exit semantics (exit 0 without selector, non-zero with) breaks no shipped skill. The 129/129b cut is at a real code boundary (readiness-deciding verbs vs terminal mutation verbs: internal/approve/impl.go, internal/executor, internal/validate's ADR-divergence ref are untouched here). `mindspec validate spec 129-readiness-tracker-honesty` at the worktree: 1 WARN only (lifecycle-binding: no epic yet — expected before approve).

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: (a) The panel-header template says to write `<your-slot>-round-1.json` beside the BRIEF; the dispatch prompt says the absolute scratch `verdict.json` — I followed the prompt. (b) The BRIEF carries unfilled `TODO(skill)` placeholders and duplicate 'Summary'/'Files in scope'/'Acceptance criteria' headings (template not fully replaced). (c) 'Deferral boundary: 234, 244' omits #250, which spec 128 handed to this follow-on by name — the BRIEF inherits the spec's own drop. (d) 'MF-3 false negatives (#239; #232 dispositioned as the same causes)' overstates the spec, which says #232 'fits cause 1 or cause 3'; per the MAJOR finding above neither fits. (e) The lens table lists nine slots (F1–F3, O1–O3, G1–G3) while the repo's CLAUDE.md describes a six-reviewer panel-run; the nine-slot spec-gate is the operator's standing protocol, so this is a doc skew, not a BRIEF error. Otherwise none found.
